sources.title: Exact v1.5 model card
sources.evidence: Names this NVIDIA Llama Nemotron release, identifies its Llama 3.3 70B Instruct base and dense NAS architecture, states July 25, 2025 release and 131072-token text context, describes updated reasoning/tool training, and links both governing NVIDIA and additional Llama agreements. Reopened the pinned card on October 27 for the parameter re-audit: 49B remains its nominal name; it does not separately specify active parameters.

sources.title: Exact v1.5 checkpoint configuration
sources.evidence: DeciLMForCausalLM, nemotron-nas, BF16, hidden width 8192, vocabulary 128256, untied embeddings, 64 query heads, 80 block configurations, 131072 positions. Exactly 49 attention blocks with 8 KV heads, 31 attention no-ops and 80 variable-width FFNs; no expert routing, linear replacements, sparsification or FFN no-ops. Fresh comparison with NVIDIA’s pinned v1.5 FP8 config found all architecture fields identical; only _name_or_path differs.

sources.title: NVIDIA checkpoint implementation
sources.evidence: Defines learned embeddings, output projection, RMSNorm, GQA projections and three-matrix SwiGLU FFNs. FFN width is ceil-to-256 of int(2*ffn_mult*hidden_size/3); skipped attention has no attention weights or input norm. RoPE inverse frequencies are nonpersistent buffers.

sources.title: Exact BF16 checkpoint tensor index
sources.evidence: Indexes 568 tensors in 21 shards and reports 99734290432 data bytes. Every indexed name was checked against configuration-derived shapes and the bounded headers. Fresh October 27 retrieval confirms the same total_size metadata; the earlier shard-header census is retained, not repeated.

sources.title: Official safetensors headers, first of 21 indexed shards
sources.evidence: Read at most 65536 bytes from each shard, requiring HTTP 206. Parsed 66712 bytes of header data in total. All 568 tensors are learned BF16 weight matrices or norms, with no scale tensors, packed elements or buffers. Shape products sum to 49867145216; all data offsets are contiguous and two bytes per element, and shard lengths match header plus data sizes.

sources.title: Exact v1.5 tokenizer and chat template
sources.evidence: The template defaults to thinking enabled, handles /no_think and /think system directives, and formats tool definitions, tool-call arrays and tool responses with dedicated delimiters. The model card separately documents training and inference support for those capabilities.

sources.title: NVIDIA tool-call parser
sources.evidence: Provides the model-specific llama_nemotron_json parser used by the card’s vLLM auto-tool-choice example; complements explicit tool training and BFCL evaluation documentation.

sources.title: NVIDIA v1.5 release article
sources.evidence: The article says it originally ran July 25, 2025 and was updated July 29. It directly names Super 49B v1.5, describes its additional post-training and links the downloadable checkpoint. It distinguishes the then-available model from the forthcoming packaged NIM microservice. Reopened for this pass; no separate v1.5 active-count specification found.

sources.title: NVIDIA Open Model License Agreement
sources.evidence: Actual agreement linked as the governing terms by the exact model card. The currently served agreement states its October 24, 2025 revision and acknowledges separately licensed components.

sources.title: Llama 3.3 Community License Agreement
sources.evidence: Actual Llama 3.3 agreement for the explicitly identified underlying model; covers use and distribution of Llama materials and derivative works. The exact v1.5 card lists this agreement as additional information.

sources.title: Llama-Nemotron technical report, September 2025 revision
sources.evidence: Reopened September 9, 2025 v5 on October 27. Its named Super checkpoint remains v1; the report does not give an explicit active-per-token count for v1.5. Its v1 nominal size is not substituted for the exact v1.5 total.

sources.title: Vultr Nemotron Super 49B deployment and HGX B200 benchmarks
sources.evidence: Original infrastructure-provider guide, updated March 11, 2026. Its Model Overview names nvidia/Llama-3_3-Nemotron-Super-49B-v1_5-FP8 and explicitly lists Active Parameters as 49B per token. It reports its own HGX B200 FP8 and BF16 measurements with serving commands and benchmark settings. This establishes Vultr’s nominal deployment convention, not a NVIDIA active-count disclosure or exact tensor census.

sources.title: NVIDIA exact v1.5 FP8 model card
sources.evidence: Pinned NVIDIA card identifies version 1.5, links the original v1.5 release, describes the same NAS-derived dense model, and supplies vLLM commands selecting ModelOpt quantization. Compared with the BF16 card and configurations, this supports treating FP8 as the precision variant of this model; it does not itself disclose active parameters.

sources.title: NVIDIA exact v1.5 FP8 checkpoint configuration
sources.evidence: Fresh JSON comparison with s2: every field is equal except _name_or_path (FP8 retains llama_nemotron_super_v1_1, BF16 says llama_nemotron_super_v1_5). Vocabulary, embeddings, all 80 block configurations, attention and FFN widths, and architecture class match. The stale internal name is outweighed by the exact repository/card identity; no learned-architecture change appears in the configurations.

sources.title: NVIDIA v1.5 FP8 quantization configuration
sources.evidence: ModelOpt metadata declares FP8 weight and KV-cache quantization, excluding lm_head. Together with matching architecture configurations and the exact card, this supports transferring the provider’s nominal model-size convention across BF16/FP8 precision variants without treating quantization metadata as learned model parameters.

name.note: Exact version from the card and repository, preserving the catalog’s spaced display spelling.

developer.note: NVIDIA supplies the NAS-derived and post-trained model; Meta supplies the Llama 3.3 base.

family.note: The exact card places this release in the Llama Nemotron collection.

release_date.note: Exact card gives this day for Hugging Face and build.nvidia.com. The contemporaneous article independently records its original July 25 publication; July 29 is a later update.

open_weights.note: Official full BF16 checkpoint is downloadable in 21 safetensors shards.

license.value: NVIDIA Open Model License + Llama 3.3 Community License
license.note: Descriptive combined label: the exact card calls the NVIDIA agreement governing terms and identifies the underlying Llama 3.3 agreement as additional information. The Apache notices in implementation code do not license the model weights as Apache.

parameters_b.note: Retain the prior verified BF16 checkpoint count of 49867145216 learned parameters (49.867145216B), including both embeddings and norms. The earlier configuration/code reconstruction matched all 568 tensor shapes and bounded shard headers. Fresh retrieval of the pinned card, config and index confirms the 49B nominal label, unchanged architecture and 99734290432 BF16 data bytes; no shard census was repeated in this pass. Prior reconstruction: 2*128256*8192 + 49*(2*8192**2+2*8192*1024) + 3*8192*1642496 + (49+80+1)*8192; FFN widths sum to 1642496. Nonpersistent RoPE buffers are excluded.

active_parameters_b.note: 49B is Vultr’s explicit nominal active-per-token convention for exact v1.5 FP8 in its original deployment/benchmark guide. NVIDIA’s FP8 and BF16 configs have identical architecture fields, with only a stale internal name differing; the card and ModelOpt metadata identify the precision variant. Apply that nominal convention to this unchanged model architecture. It is not a NVIDIA direct active-count disclosure or an exact measure of every tensor’s participation; the independently established total remains 49.867145216B. Fresh NVIDIA-card, release-article and family-report searches found no separate v1.5 active count.

architecture.note: Dense decoder-only Transformer derived through NAS. This exact checkpoint has 80 slots, 49 full GQA blocks and 31 attention skips, plus 80 SwiGLU FFNs of six widths. It has no MoE routing, linear attention substitutions or FFN no-ops. Do not transfer the Ultra FFN-fusion structure to this model.

context_window.note: Both input/output specification and max_position_embeddings give 131072. The card’s 65536-token vLLM command is a chosen serving example, not the model maximum.

modalities.note: Exact card specifies text input and output; checkpoint is a causal language model.

reasoning.note: Documented reasoning post-training and selectable reasoning behavior. The v1.5 template defaults to thinking enabled and processes /no_think; this is directly verified for v1.5.

tool_call.note: Explicit tool-training and BFCL evaluation, supported template, supplied parser and working-format serving instructions establish model support beyond inherited template syntax alone.

description.value: NVIDIA’s NAS-derived Llama 3.3 model, updated in v1.5 with supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning for reasoning, chat and tool calling.
description.note: Replaces vague efficiency and specialized-agent claims with the documented derivation and training purpose.

patch.license: NVIDIA Open Model License + Llama 3.3 Community License
patch.description: NVIDIA’s NAS-derived Llama 3.3 model, updated in v1.5 with supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning for reasoning, chat and tool calling.
patch.notes: Total is the exact 49.867145216B BF16 checkpoint count; 49B is nominal. Active 49B follows Vultr’s nominal deployment convention for v1.5 FP8, whose architecture matches BF16; NVIDIA does not separately disclose an active count. The NAS architecture has 49 attention blocks, 31 attention skips and 80 variable-width dense FFNs. Reasoning defaults on; /no_think disables it. Both NVIDIA and Llama 3.3 licenses apply.
